name: Pelikan Hi-Vis Safety Shell
description:
There is nothing subtle about this jacket and that is entirely the point. The Pelikan Hi-Vis Safety Shell is a Class 3 high-visibility rain jacket in ANSI-equivalent fluorescent yellow-green, with retroreflective silver tape at the chest, back, and arms in the standard chevron pattern. It is a lightweight shell, wind- and water-resistant, with a mesh lining and a hood that adjusts with a single cord. The Pelikan logo is small and on the chest. Everything else is light.

This is the jacket of infrastructure workers, road crews, site safety monitors, and dock workers across the Great Lakes corridor. It is also worn by anyone who needs to be seen in the dark — Shelf residents navigating dangerous transit routes sometimes wear hi-vis ironically or earnestly, as visibility is survival in certain parts of the city. Pelikan makes good shells at a working price. The reflective tape on this model catches light from a hundred meters.
what_it_says: You work outside or in hazardous conditions, or you have decided that being seen is more important than being fashionable. In the right context, this is also a kind of uniform.
worn_by: people who want to be visible in low light
story_hooks: A character uses a Pelikan hi-vis to move through a Shelf construction zone without challenge — workers in hi-vis are invisible in plain sight
Someone is using the reflective tape pattern to send coded signals; different tape configurations on different workers form a message visible from a drone overhead
A Tier 5 fashion label releases a runway piece clearly inspired by the Pelikan hi-vis; the infrastructure workers whose uniform it copies find this both flattering and enraging
related_entities: Tethered Orbital Reconnaissance and Suppression Drone TORSD-7 'Kitestring'

physical_description.visual_profile: A strikingly bright, unambiguous presence on any wearer—the jacket demands visibility from every angle. The silhouette is straightforward and utilitarian: a slightly oversized, boxy cut that prioritizes function over form. Retroreflective chevron stripes running across chest, back, and arms create a geometric, almost target-like pattern that catches and throws back light with unsettling intensity. The wearer becomes a beacon.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, oversized cut designed to layer over work clothes or light augmentation rigs. Generous arm mobility for reach-heavy labor. Dropped shoulder line. Hood sits loose and adjustable.
physical_description.primary_material: Lightweight ripstop nylon shell with wind and water resistance. Breathable mesh lining to prevent sweat buildup during active work. Non-insulated.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly waxy synthetic exterior that sheds water. Fine mesh lining visible at cuffs and hood opening. Retroreflective tape has a subtle bumped texture that optimizes light reflection.
physical_description.color_scheme: ANSI-compliant fluorescent yellow-green as primary color—a sickly-bright hue that practically vibrates against dark urban backgrounds. Silver-white retroreflective chevron stripes in standard high-visibility pattern (two horizontal stripes across torso, one around each arm). Pelikan wordmark in small dark gray at left chest.
physical_description.closures: Full-length front zip with durable plastic pull tab. Hood drawcord with single-point adjustment. Velcro cuff adjusters at wrists. No collar fastener—hood drapes open when not deployed.
distinctive_features: Retroreflective chevron striping meets ANSI 107-2015 Class 3 standards
Reflective tape visible from 100+ meters in headlight or flashlight beam
Mesh lining visible at interior—speaks to ventilation priority
Adjustable hood with single drawcord—fast deployment in rain
Minimal branding: small Pelikan chest logo only
Lightweight construction prioritizes packability over durability
Slightly translucent quality to fluorescent material under certain light angles
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional / Tier 4 working-class infrastructure tool. Affordable, mass-produced, utilitarian. No luxury markers.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of necessity. Road crews, dock workers, site safety monitors across the GLMZ wear this daily. Increasingly adopted by Shelf residents and unlicensed transit workers in ungoverned zones—visibility as survival strategy. Also worn ironically by corpo workers slumming in lower districts. The jacket announces: *I am working. I am visible. I exist.*
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually broken-in and weathered. Scuffs on synthetic exterior from work contact. Possible tape repairs where reflective patches have been re-glued after heavy wear. Lining may be slightly faded and pilled. Reflective strips show accumulated grime that dulls their shine until next cleaning.

image_prompt: A figure in a sickly-bright fluorescent yellow-green safety jacket stands under cold gray industrial lighting in a rain-slicked urban corridor, wet pavement reflecting streaks of reflected chevron tape. The retroreflective stripes glow with aggressive silver-white intensity under directional light sources. Moody, desaturated background of concrete brutalism and dark metal scaffolding. The wearer is sharp and centered; the jacket dominates the frame with its utilitarian, almost hostile visibility. Shot from mid-torso to head. --ar 2:3 --v 6
